problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: 'Large language models (LLMs) suffer from proactive interference (PI): previously processed but now-outdated information in the context window disrupts retrieval of current, relevant values.' [SleepGate Abstract, p.1, L12-13]. The paper insists this is not a context-length problem: 'This finding reveals a working memory bottleneck that is fundamentally distinct from context length limitations. The model can see the relevant tokens—the difficulty is suppressing the irrelevant ones.' [SleepGate §1, p.2, L57-58]
problem_stated.the_mechanistic_diagnosis: 'In the standard transformer attention mechanism, every entry in the key-value cache participates in every attention computation with no mechanism for selective inhibition. As stale entries accumulate, they collectively drown out the signal from current, relevant entries through sheer numerical mass.' [SleepGate §1, p.2, L58-61]. This sentence is the paper's real thesis: the missing capability is an inhibition lever inside softmax, not a memory.
problem_stated.the_operational_question: Given a KV cache in which many entries refer to the same semantic slot and only the last one is current, can a learned, content-dependent per-entry modifier suppress the stale ones — and can that modifier be trained end-to-end alongside the language-modelling objective? [SleepGate §1.2, p.2-3, L92-107; §4, p.8, L472-474]
problem_stated.the_inherited_empirical_claim: The whole problem statement is downstream of one prior result: 'Wang & Sun [2025] recently provided a clear demonstration of this phenomenon... retrieval accuracy declines log-linearly toward zero as the number of prior (now-superseded) associations increases. The errors are not random—models systematically retrieve overwritten values' [SleepGate §1, p.2, L49-55], citing Wang, C. & Sun, J. V. (2025), 'Unable to forget: Proactive interference reveals working memory limits in LLMs beyond context length', arXiv:2506.08184 [SleepGate References, p.18, L1127-1128].
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] The problem statement is well posed and the diagnosis in §1 is correct as a statement about softmax. The gap between that diagnosis and what the paper actually builds is where every problem in this note lives: the diagnosis names a READ-side defect (no inhibition lever in attention) and the paper correctly builds a READ-side fix (an additive pre-softmax bias), but then dresses the fix in write-side vocabulary — sleep, consolidation, eviction, forgetting — that its evaluated configuration never performs.

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: SleepGate instantiates none of (U-W), (U-Θ), (U-E). In the soft-biasing configuration that produced every reported number it modifies the READ map of (R) by inserting a learned, content-dependent additive pre-softmax bias over the KV cache (its Eq. 11 replaces its Eq. 1); the only state it persistently mutates is the KV cache itself, and in that configuration the mutation reduces to a deterministic, parameter-free key decay whose isolated contribution the paper's own ablation measures at baseline level.
core_mechanism.the_two_variants_must_never_be_conflated: The paper specifies two systems and evaluates only one. Algorithm 1 splits at line 16: lines 1-15 (key decay + gate scoring) are common; lines 16-21 are the '— Soft Biasing Variant (used in experiments) —' and return an attention bias vector; lines 22-33 are the '— Hard Eviction Variant (Phases 3-5) —' and return a modified cache. [SleepGate Algorithm 1, p.22, L1309-1358]. Figure 1's caption states the same split: 'In the soft biasing variant used in our experiments, the cache passes through decay and the forgetting gate, and the resulting retention scores are converted to additive attention biases (Eq. 10) for a second forward pass. In the hard eviction variant, entries additionally pass through consolidation before eviction.' [SleepGate Figure 1 caption, p.4, L163-168]. §6.3 confirms the soft variant was used and that Stage 3 threshold calibration was skipped [SleepGate §6.3, p.11, L707-711]. EVERY statement in this note distinguishes the two, because the paper's theory (§5), its consolidation module (§3.4), its eviction rule (Eq. 6) and its three-way Gumbel head (Eq. 8-9) all belong to the variant that was never run.

equations_unified.latex: \hat y \;=\; f\big(q;\ \Theta,\ \varnothing,\ \varnothing\big),\qquad \mathrm{Attn}(q_t,\mathcal{K})=\sum_{i=1}^{t}\frac{\exp(q_t^\top k_i/\sqrt d)}{\sum_{j=1}^{t}\exp(q_t^\top k_j/\sqrt d)}\,v_i
equations_unified.gloss: Standard causal attention over the KV cache. In the book's frame the second and third slots of (R) are EMPTY: there are no fast weights and there is no external store. Everything this paper does happens inside the first slot's read.

Each entry gains four metadata fields: its own position, a slot signature $m_i\in\mathbb{R}^{64}$, a binary superseded flag $u_i$, and the cumulative attention it has received. The last field is the H2O heavy-hitter statistic, imported as an input feature to the very gate that is supposed to beat H2O.

The tagger is a single learned projection with a local-pooled context window ($h_{\text{pool}}=4$, $\delta=0.85$). An entry is flagged superseded if any LATER entry lands in the same slot. Amortised $O(1)$ per token via LSH is claimed but never measured.

A 2-layer MLP scores each cache entry. All of its parameters live in $\Theta$ — they are trained in the outer loop and frozen at test time. Nothing about $\pi_i$ is a state update; it is a function evaluation on the current cache.

equations_unified.id: SG-5 (the biased read) — THIS IS THE PAPER'S ACTUAL MECHANISM
equations_unified.gloss: The read map changes and nothing else does. Because $\psi_i$ enters the logit additively and $\psi_i=\beta_{\text{bias}}\log\pi_i$, the softmax numerator is multiplied by $\pi_i^{\beta_{\text{bias}}}$ — i.e. this is exactly a learned multiplicative reweighting of the attention distribution, $\mathrm{Attn}_{\text{sleep}}\propto\sum_i \pi_i^{\beta_{\text{bias}}}\exp(q_t^\top k_i/\sqrt d)v_i$. [note-writer] Stating it that way makes the classification unavoidable: it is a reweighting of a read, in the same formal family as ALiBi/relative-position biases and as H2O's masking, differing only in that the weights are produced by a learned content-dependent head instead of a fixed rule.

equations_unified.id: SG-6 (the only persistent mutation in the evaluated variant)
equations_unified.gloss: Key decay, Algorithm 1 Phase 1, executed in BOTH variants. Compare with (U-W): $W_t=\alpha_t W_{t-1}+S_t$. SG-6 is formally $\alpha_t$ applied entry-wise with $S_t\equiv0$ — a retention factor with the surprise term deleted, applied to a SET of vectors rather than to a fixed-shape operator. That is why it is not (U-W): (U-W)'s defining content is the $-\eta_t\nabla_W\ell$ term, and nothing in this paper computes an inner loss at test time.

what_is_NOT_in_the_mechanism: NO external store. There is no $E$, no record, no index, no retrieval, no persistence beyond the request. $\mathrm{ret}(E,q)$ has no referent in this paper.

NO fast weights. There is no fixed-shape recurrent state and no inner loss. The paper makes the absence a selling point: 'SleepGate occupies a middle ground: it preserves the random-access property of the KV cache while adding selective forgetting' [SleepGate §8.2, p.15, L929-930].
NO weight update at inference. $\Theta$ — including the gate, tagger and consolidation parameters — is frozen after training. Every 'learned' claim in the paper is an outer-loop claim.

NO persistence across queries. Each evaluated episode contains exactly one query [SleepGate §6.2, p.11, L697-700]. $N_q=1$ by construction, so the amortisation identity (A) has no denominator and cannot be exercised.

NO consolidation in any reported number. Module 3 (33,152 parameters, 26.7% of the paper's own 'sleep overhead') is counted in Table 1 but is unreachable in the soft-biasing variant and receives no gradient during Stage 2.
NO pre-trained model, no natural language, no real corpus. A 793,344-parameter transformer trained from scratch on a 1024-token synthetic vocabulary [SleepGate §6.1, p.11, L663-665].

outer_vs_inner.reader_takeaway: Read the rows in order and the classification falls out mechanically. Rows 1-5 are $\Theta$ and move only during training. Rows 6-7 are functions, not state. Row 8 is the only persistent test-time mutation and it is a fixed arithmetic shrink. Rows 12-13 are empty. There is no row in which a layer of the three-layer partition changes state before a query.

update_layer.instantiates: NONE of (U-W), (U-Θ), (U-E) at test time. The training-time optimisation of $\Theta$ (including $G_\theta$) is ordinary outer-loop learning on the training-epoch clock, which every paper in the corpus does and which the discriminant's step 3 sends to 'not a sleep round'.
canonical_forms_and_why_each_fails: (U-E): $E_{k+1}=\mathrm{wr}(E_k,\hat c_k)$ — there is no $E$. No record is written, no store exists, nothing survives the request. The bias vector $\psi$ is not a record: it is not stored, not indexed, not retrieved, and is discarded by Algorithm 1's caller.

(U-Θ): $\Theta_{k+1}=\Theta_k-\eta_\Theta\nabla_\Theta\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{R}_k;\Theta_k)$ — $\Theta$ moves only during training. The deployment artifact is fixed. There is no $\mathcal{R}_k$, no self-generated training set, no sleep round index $k$.

(U-W): $W_t=\alpha_t W_{t-1}+S_t$, $S_t=\beta_t S_{t-1}-\eta_t\nabla_W\ell(W_{t-1};k_t,v_t)$ — there is no $W$. The nearest object is SG-6, key decay, which is $\alpha_t$ with $S_t\equiv0$ applied entry-wise to a growing set. (U-W)'s content is the surprise term; delete it and what remains is not a memory update but a fixed forgetting schedule. The book's own $W$-경로 판별식 (→ ch17 §17.4.1) requires (U-W) to be EXECUTED on a separate clock, not merely for its retention factor to be borrowed.
update_layer.what_it_actually_changes: The READ map. Its Eq. 11 replaces its Eq. 1: $\mathrm{Attn}_{\text{sleep}}\propto\sum_i \pi_i^{\beta_{\text{bias}}}\exp(q_t^\top k_i/\sqrt d)\,v_i$. In the book's frame this is a modification of $f(\cdot)$ in (R), leaving all three write rules untouched. This is exactly the pattern ch11 §11.2.3 names when it explains what condition (3) blocks — '읽기를 바꾼 논문이 쓰기를 바꾼 논문으로 둔갑한다' — and which it illustrates with Memory Caching.

where_does_KV_cache_compression_belong_t.verdict: The KV cache is a FOURTH state. It must not be folded into $W$. SleepGate's operation on it is a change to (R), not a fourth update rule, so the book gains a state but not a path.
where_does_KV_cache_compression_belong_t.reason_1_the_book_already_does_this_ad_h: ch17's own layer table carries a row '| KV cache $K_t,V_t$ | 비모수 상태 |' — a bin that exists nowhere in ch01's three-layer partition and nowhere in STC-STYLE-NOTATION §1.2. The book has therefore already been using a fourth category, silently, in the one chapter where a KV cache had to be classified. SleepGate is the paper that makes that silence load-bearing, because here the KV cache is not a side object but the entire subject.
where_does_KV_cache_compression_belong_t.reason_2_capacity_scales_in_a_different_: ch26 판정 1-2 rests on the three capacity expressions being functions of DIFFERENT variables — $E\propto n$, $\Theta_{\text{delta}}\propto r\,d\,L_{\text{layer}}$, $W\propto d^2 L_{\text{layer}}$ (식 (26-1)) — and derives the memory-tier placement from those exponents. A KV cache is $2\,d\,L\,L_{\text{layer}}$: it scales in sequence length $L$, a fourth variable that appears in none of the three. Folding it into $W$ would put a length-dependent object into a length-independent row and break the exponent argument that ch26's 판정 2 is built on.
where_does_KV_cache_compression_belong_t.reason_3_the_access_pattern_is_the_paper: $W$ is read by a single operator application over the whole state; a KV cache is randomly addressable per entry. The paper makes precisely this the definition of its position: 'SleepGate occupies a middle ground: it preserves the random-access property of the KV cache while adding selective forgetting' [SleepGate §8.2, p.15, L929-930]. Classifying it as $W$ would erase the distinction the paper itself is organised around.
where_does_KV_cache_compression_belong_t.reason_4_the_Rosetta_row_survives_but_ne: STC-STYLE-NOTATION §3 teaches 'KV cache ↔ $W$: KV는 append-only 무손실, $W$는 고정 크기 손실 압축'. SleepGate erodes exactly one of the two differentiae — under the hard variant the cache becomes lossy and bounded (Prop. 1), and even under the soft variant it stops being untouched (SG-6). The other differentia — fixed-shape, weight-shaped, non-addressable — is untouched. So the row is not overturned; it must gain a caveat saying the append-only/lossless half is a design choice rather than a property of caches. See book_impact.
alternatives_considered_and_rejected: Fold into $W$ because the augmented metadata plus decayed keys look like 'session state'. REJECTED: they are per-entry rather than per-model, recomputed rather than accumulated, and carry no gradient or surprise term. Accepting this would also admit H2O, StreamingLLM and every eviction policy into the $W$-path, which would raise the $W$-path sample from 1 to dozens for the wrong reason and destroy ch27 판정 3.

Fold into $E$ because the bias is a 'learned context' $\hat c$. REJECTED: $\hat c$ in (U-E) is a record produced by offline inference and consumed by later queries through $\mathrm{ret}$. $\psi$ is none of those — no store, no retrieval, no persistence.

Create a fourth PATH ($\mathcal{K}$-경로) alongside $E$/$W$/$\Theta$. REJECTED, and this is the finer judgment. A path in this book is defined by which UPDATE RULE it executes (→ STC-STYLE-NOTATION §1.6, '판별식' column). SleepGate executes no update rule; it edits the read. Creating a path for it would grant an update-rule-shaped status to a read-side method and would let every attention-mask paper into the taxonomy. The correct move is smaller and stricter: register the KV cache as a fourth STATE in the ledger, note that operations on it are (R)-side unless a paper shows a state that survives to a later query, and leave the three paths at three.
where_does_KV_cache_compression_belong_t.the_one_configuration_that_would_change_: The hard-eviction variant, actually run, with cycles firing before the query, would produce a cache that (a) persists to later queries within the same request and (b) has been modified by a $B_s>0$ procedure. That configuration would still not be $E$/$W$/$\Theta$ — it would be the first genuine instance of an offline update to the fourth state, and the book would have to decide whether condition (3) is a statement about THREE layers or about ANY state. See discriminant_verdict.the_third_grey_zone.

update_layer.ordering: Within one forward pass at position $t$: wake pass computes $(k_t,v_t)$ and logits → signature $m_t$ and conflict flags $u_j$ are set → entry appended → $\mathrm{trigger}(t)$ evaluated → if fired, key decay mutates all $k_i$, the gate scores all entries, the bias $\psi$ is formed, and attention is re-run. There is no phase in which the model is idle, no phase in which no query is pending, and no state that crosses a request boundary.

discriminant_verdict.deciding_condition: (3) 대상. No state in $\Theta$, $W$ or $E$ changes at any point in the evaluated system. This is decisive on its own and does not depend on how condition (1) is resolved.
discriminant_verdict.one_line: SleepGate is the second paper in the corpus to be excluded by condition (3) for changing the read equation instead of a write rule — and the first to be excluded by condition (3) while wearing the vocabulary of every other condition.

conditions.condition: (1) 시계 — does the state-changing operation execute BEFORE the query arrives?
conditions.verdict: INDETERMINATE as specified; FAILS as evaluated.
conditions.as_specified: Eq. 16's trigger is a function of the token index $t$ inside the ongoing stream, and Algorithm 2 line 12 gates the sleep phase on $\mathrm{trigger}(t)$. In a PI-LLM episode the updates precede the query, so a cycle firing during the update stream would be 'before the query'. On the specification alone, condition (1) is satisfiable.
conditions.as_evaluated: The paper says the sleep path runs on EVERY forward pass, not on a trigger: 'every forward pass computes both unbiased (wake) and soft-biased (sleep) logits' [SleepGate §4.2 Stage 2, p.9, L565-567] and 'Each forward pass produces both unbiased logits (for the wake loss) and soft-biased logits (for the sleep loss)' [§6.3, p.11, L715-717]. Table 2's caption states the reported numbers are read off the biased pass: 'SleepGate uses post-sleep (soft-biased) evaluation.' [Table 2 caption, p.12, L721-723]. So the bias that produces the result is computed and applied AT the query position, from features that include the query-time cache. On what was measured, the state-changing (read-changing) operation and the query are the same event.
conditions.why_it_cannot_be_settled: The paper never reports how many micro-cycles fired, at which positions, or under which of the three trigger arms. §4.2/§6.3 and Algorithm 2 line 12 directly contradict each other on whether the trigger gates anything at all. See unfavorable_facts UF-6 and todo_verify TV-1.
conditions.note_writer_arithmetic: [본서 산술] With $T_{\text{cyc}}^{\max}=128$ tokens [Table 3] and episodes of $n_{\text{PI}}\le30$ updates, the periodic fallback arm can never fire inside an evaluated episode unless an update consumes more than ~4 tokens — the paper does not state tokens-per-update, so this is conditional. See todo_verify TV-2.

conditions.verdict: PASSES for the gate+re-read component; FAILS for the component that persists.
conditions.detail: The gate is a genuine extra forward pass over the whole cache, and the paper says so: 'Each sleep micro-cycle requires a forward pass through the gate network for every cache entry. For a cache of size C and a gate with $d_h=128$ hidden units, this is $O(C\cdot d_g\cdot d_h)$ per cycle—negligible compared to a transformer forward pass, but non-zero.' [SleepGate §8.5, p.16, L973-976]. On top of that, Algorithm 1 line 20 re-runs attention with the bias, and Figure 1's caption calls it 'a second forward pass'. So $B_s>0$ in an absolute sense.
conditions.the_split_that_matters: The component that persists (SG-6 key decay) is a parameter-free elementwise scalar multiply — arithmetic, not inference. Under the book's application step 4 ('저장·복사·색인만 한다면 $B_s=0$'), a fixed arithmetic transform with no learned content-dependence sits on the $B_s\approx0$ side. The component with $B_s>0$ (the gate and the biased re-read) leaves nothing behind. NO SINGLE COMPONENT OF SLEEPGATE SATISFIES BOTH (2) AND (3)-with-(4).
conditions.the_deeper_point: Because the whole mechanism runs inside inference, whatever it costs is charged to $L_w$, not to $B_s$. The book's touchstone — 'sleep은 정의상 $L_w$에 0을 기여한다' (→ ch11 §11.2.3, → ch01 표 1-4) — is violated in the opposite direction from MemGPT: MemGPT spends decode budget inside the user turn, SleepGate spends attention budget inside the same forward pass.

conditions.condition: (3) 대상 — does a layer among $\Theta$/$W$/$E$ actually change state?
conditions.verdict: FAILS. This is the deciding condition.
conditions.detail: $\Theta$ is frozen after training (including $G_\theta$, $P_m$, $P_K$, $P_V$). $W$ does not exist — the architecture has no fast weights, and §8.2 positions the method against the fixed-size-state family. $E$ does not exist — there is no store, no record, no retrieval. What changes is the KV cache: decayed keys in the soft variant, evicted/consolidated entries in the hard variant that was never run. The KV cache is not one of the three layers (see update_layer.where_does_KV_cache_compression_belong_the_judgment).
conditions.the_sharper_form: Even granting the KV cache the status of a layer, the evaluated variant fails: under soft biasing the effective mechanism does not modify the cache at all. It computes $\psi_i$ from the cache and re-runs attention. Eq. 11 differs from Eq. 1 by a term that lives in the read. This is the Memory Caching pattern verbatim — ch11 §11.2.3: '갱신 규칙은 baseline과 글자 그대로 같고... 바뀐 것은 읽기'.
conditions.the_residue: The one thing that both persists and changes is SG-6 key decay. Its isolated contribution is measured by the paper: the Decay Only ablation reaches at most 12.5% across all depths and 'performs comparably to other baselines' [SleepGate §7.2, p.13, L861-864]. So the persistent change is, by the paper's own ablation, worth nothing.

conditions.condition: (4) 소비자 — is the changed state consumed by a LATER query?
conditions.verdict: FAILS as evaluated; unresolvable as specified.
conditions.detail: Each evaluated episode contains exactly one query ('followed by a query for the most recent value' [SleepGate §6.2, p.11, L697-700]), so there is no later query anywhere in the experiments — $N_q=1$ by construction. Within a request, Algorithm 1's soft branch returns $\psi$ and the caller consumes it immediately (line 20-21); nothing about $\psi$ is carried forward, and it is a pure function of the current cache, so it is recomputed rather than reused. The decayed keys do survive to the next position, but see (3)'s residue.
conditions.contrast_with_MemGPT: MemGPT fails only (1): its writes are real, persistent, and consumed by later turns. SleepGate fails (3) and (4) and is indeterminate on (1). It is therefore NOT a boundary case in MemGPT's sense and must not be filed as one.

the_third_grey_zone.claim: ch11 §11.2.4 states that the discriminant has exactly two grey zones ('회색지대가 둘 있고, 둘 다 의도된 것이다'): clock-less papers, and condition (2) being an inequality. SleepGate exposes a THIRD, and it is not intended.
the_third_grey_zone.what_it_is: Step 2 of the application procedure — '좌변을 세 층에 배정한다. 배포 아티팩트의 일부이면 $\Theta$, 요청·세션에 붙는 가중치 형태의 상태이면 $W$, 모델 밖 레코드이면 $E$다' — is not exhaustive over states. A KV cache is a per-request state that is neither weight-shaped nor outside the model, so step 2 has no bin for it and the procedure routes it to failure at step 2 rather than at a named condition. The verdict comes out right and the reason is not printed.
the_third_grey_zone.why_it_matters: Without naming it, the book cannot distinguish two very different exclusions: 'this paper changes nothing' (true of Memory Layers post-deployment) and 'this paper changes something the book does not model' (true of SleepGate). ch11 must say the second out loud, because the second is the class into which the entire KV-cache-management literature falls — H2O, StreamingLLM, sliding window, SnapKV, PagedAttention eviction, quantised caches — and this reader lives in that literature.
the_third_grey_zone.does_it_falsify_the_discriminant: NO. ch11 §11.2.4's own falsification condition is '네 조건을 모두 만족하는데 이 책이 배제한 절차가 발견되면'. SleepGate does not satisfy all four. The discriminant survives; its documentation is incomplete.

B_s.detail: No sleep budget in any absolute unit appears anywhere. Grep over the full text: 'FLOP' 0 hits, 'wall-clock' 0 hits, 'latency' 0 hits, 'throughput' 0 hits. What the paper does print is (i) one asymptotic expression, '$O(C\cdot d_g\cdot d_h)$ per cycle—negligible compared to a transformer forward pass, but non-zero' [SleepGate §8.5, p.16, L973-976], and (ii) a PARAMETER overhead of 15.6% in Table 1 [p.11, L666-693], which is a storage figure and not a compute figure. Table 1's own label — 'Sleep overhead 15.6%' — invites the misreading, so the chapter must relabel it 파라미터 오버헤드.
B_s.what_the_paper_s_own_overhead_account_om: Algorithm 1 line 20 ('Re-run attention with additive bias b (Eq. 11)') and Figure 1's caption ('for a second forward pass') both mandate a re-read that §8.5's overhead paragraph does not count. §8.5 counts only the gate MLP.
B_s.note_writer_arithmetic: [본서 산술] At the paper's own configuration ($L=1024$, 4 layers, $d=128$, causal attention, non-embedding matmul parameters $793{,}344-131{,}072=662{,}272$): one full sequence forward costs $\approx2.43\times10^{9}$ FLOPs, of which attention is $\approx1.07\times10^{9}$ and matmuls $\approx1.36\times10^{9}$. Re-running attention only adds $\approx+44\%$; a full second forward pass adds $+100\%$; the gate over all $C=1024$ entries ($2\cdot C\cdot d_g\cdot d_h$ with $d_g=578$, $d_h=128$) adds $\approx+6.2\%$. So the true compute overhead of the EVALUATED configuration is between roughly +50% and +106% per pass, not the 15.6% that Table 1's label suggests and not 'negligible'. These are lower bounds on the ratio's magnitude, stated as form not value — the paper prints no measurement to compare against.
B_s.finding: This is the fourth corpus paper (after Letta STC, SCM, `Do LMs Need Sleep?`) to leave the numerator of the amortisation argument empty, and it is the first to leave it empty while HAVING a fully specified, tiny, reproducible cost model — 917,313 parameters, one architecture, one sequence length. Everything needed to print $B_s$ in FLOPs is in Table 1 and §6.1. It is not printed. That strengthens ch24 §24.3.1's judgment that the silence is about reporting convention rather than measurement difficulty (→ ch26 판정 6).

L_w.value: absent — and structurally, this paper's cost IS $L_w$
L_w.detail: No wall-clock, TTFT, ms/token or ITL figure appears. The word 'latency' does not occur in the paper at all (0 hits), which is unusual even by this corpus's standards — Letta STC at least used latency rhetorically in motivation.
L_w.the_structural_statement: [note-writer] Because every module executes inside the ongoing forward pass ('These components are activated periodically during inference in "sleep micro-cycles"' [SleepGate Abstract, p.1, L22-23]), the gate pass and the attention re-run are charged to the wake path by construction. The book's touchstone is that sleep contributes 0 to $L_w$ (→ ch11 §11.2.3, → ch01 표 1-4). Here the entire cost lands on $L_w$ and none on $B_s$. That single sentence is an alternative route to the same verdict as condition (1)'s failure, and it is the form a systems reader will find most convincing.
L_w.proxy_values_actually_reported: None. Not even a token-count proxy of the kind Letta STC used. The only quantitative axis anywhere in the paper is PI depth.

C_cap.value: absent in bytes; UNIQUELY IN THIS CORPUS, reported as a bound in entries
C_cap.detail: Proposition 1 states $|\mathcal{K}'^+|\le T_{\text{cyc}}/(\phi_e+(1-\phi_e)(1-1/\gamma_{\text{comp}}))$ [SleepGate §5.3 Eq. 25, p.10, L635-648]. That is a steady-state state-capacity bound — the only one in the corpus. But: (a) the unit is cache ENTRIES, not bytes, and no dtype is stated anywhere in the paper; (b) it applies to the hard-eviction variant, which was never run; (c) it has no proof, not even a sketch; (d) its own printed numerical instantiation is wrong (see unfavorable_facts UF-11).
C_cap.what_a_byte_figure_would_require_and_whe: The augmented cache (Eq. 2) adds four metadata fields per entry — position, a 64-dim slot signature, a binary flag, and a scalar attention accumulator — and the paper never prices any of them.
C_cap.note_writer_arithmetic: [본서 산술] Reconstructing from the parameter counts (see experiments.parameter_reconstruction), the tagger's projection is $P_m\in\mathbb{R}^{64\times256}$, which requires a 128-wide input key, so the slot signature is computed ONCE PER TOKEN at model width and is shared across all 4 layers and 4 heads — it is not per-(layer,head). Under that reading and bf16: base KV per token = $2\times128\times2\,\mathrm{B}\times4\ \text{layers}=2048$ B; metadata per token $\approx 64\times2 + 4 + 1 + 2 = 135$ B, i.e. $\approx+6.6\%$. If instead the signature were materialised per (layer, head) as Eq. 2's scoping over $C^{\ell,h}$ literally implies, the same figure would be $16\times$ larger and the metadata would dominate the cache. The paper does not resolve which. See todo_verify TV-3.
C_cap.finding: The obligatory caveat 'corpus 전체에서 상태 용량을 바이트로 보고한 논문이 0편이다' (ch26 판정 6, PRE-RESEARCH §4) SURVIVES — no bytes here either. But the caveat's wording should be tightened: this paper bounds the state in entries, so the honest form is '바이트로 보고한 논문이 0편이고, 어떤 단위로든 상태를 상한한 논문은 1편이다'.

rho.detail: There is no round index anywhere. One pass, one episode, one query, one evaluation. Repeated consolidation is proposed only as future work: 'applying multi-round sleep cycles may address this limitation' [SleepGate §8.5, p.15, L960-962]. So $\rho$ is excluded by construction, exactly as in Letta STC.

is_proactive_interference_the_same_as_rh.answer: No. They are distinct quantities on the two different sides of this book's frame, and they are near-duals rather than variants.
is_proactive_interference_the_same_as_rh.axis: $\rho$ is a WRITE-side quantity — 라운드당 성능 손실, the damage the state takes from being rewritten. It attaches to (U-W)/(U-Θ)/(U-E) and is indexed by the sleep round $k$. PI is a READ-side quantity — the loss of retrieval precision caused by a state that retained too much. It attaches to (R) and is indexed by the update count $n_{\text{PI}}$.
is_proactive_interference_the_same_as_rh.what_is_damaged: Under $\rho$, the thing you wanted to keep degrades. Under PI nothing stored degrades — every entry is intact and byte-perfect, and that is precisely the problem. The paper says so: 'The model can see the relevant tokens—the difficulty is suppressing the irrelevant ones.' [SleepGate §1, p.2, L57-58]. $\rho$ is a pathology of lossy retention; PI is a pathology of LOSSLESS retention.
is_proactive_interference_the_same_as_rh.the_shape_coincidence_that_makes_the_con: Both degrade monotonically in a round-like index — $\rho$ in $k$, PI in $n_{\text{PI}}$ (log-linear in Wang & Sun; $\approx1/n$ in this paper's Eq. 22). Anyone plotting the two curves side by side would see the same shape. The shape is the same and the mechanism is opposite, so the identification must be refused explicitly rather than left to the reader.
is_proactive_interference_the_same_as_rh.how_they_are_related_and_this_is_where_t: They are the two ends of one trade-off. The cure for PI is deliberately inducing loss, and the paper names the price of that cure using the book's own concept: 'Over-Forgetting. The soft attention biasing approach partially mitigates the risk of over-forgetting compared to hard eviction: entries are downweighted, not deleted, allowing the model to recover if the gate makes errors. However, the risk remains for entries with very low retention scores, where the bias is effectively $-\infty$.' [SleepGate §8.5, p.15, L963-966]. So in this paper $\rho$ appears as the COST of reducing PI, never as PI itself. Any mechanism that resolves PI by forgetting buys a read-axis gain by taking on a write-axis risk — and this paper's own failure mode at $n_{\text{PI}}\ge15$ is the read-axis side of that ledger, not the write-axis side.
is_proactive_interference_the_same_as_rh.ledger_consequence: The book's cost quadruple has a symbol for degradation-from-lossy-writing ($\rho$) and none for degradation-from-accumulation. That gap was invisible while the corpus contained no paper whose subject was accumulation. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT create a fifth cost symbol — STC-STYLE-NOTATION §1.2 P4 forbids it ('비용 기호는 §1.2의 4종 외에 신설하지 않는다') and a B군 paper cannot justify amending the global cost table. Instead (i) register the distinction as a CONCEPT in the ledger (see concept_ledger_delta), (ii) use $\rho_{\text{conf}}$ note-locally for this paper's conflict density, and (iii) state the gap plainly in ch11 or ch18 rather than papering over it.
is_proactive_interference_the_same_as_rh.one_more_asymmetry_worth_printing: $\rho$ is measured by re-testing OLD material after new writes (the book's $\Pi$ matrix, BWT). PI is measured by testing the NEWEST material in the presence of old. The two experiments are mirror images: $\rho$ holds the query fixed and grows the write history; PI holds the write history's target fixed at the most recent item and grows the distractor count. A single experiment cannot report both.

N_q.detail: 'Each episode consists of a stream of key-value update tokens for a single entity: $(e,v_1),(e,v_2),\dots,(e,v_n)$, followed by a query for the most recent value.' [SleepGate §6.2, p.11, L697-700]. One query per episode. The amortisation identity (A) has denominator 1, so $C_{\text{avg}}=C_{\text{wake}}+C_{\text{sleep}}$ and no amortisation is possible even in principle. The paper never mentions amortisation, reuse across queries, or cost sharing — consistent with, and a further confirmation of, its not being in this category.

parameter_reconstruction.status: [본서 산술] Every figure in Table 1 reconstructs EXACTLY from §6.1's configuration. This is a genuine point in the paper's favour and it is also how several architectural facts the paper never states can be recovered.
parameter_reconstruction.base: per layer: attention $4\times(128\times128)+4\times128=66{,}048$; FFN $128{\cdot}256+256+256{\cdot}128+128=65{,}920$; two LayerNorms $512$ → 132,480. $\times4=529{,}920$. Plus embedding $1024{\cdot}128=131{,}072$, LM head $128{\cdot}1024+1024=132{,}096$, final LayerNorm 256 → 793,344 EXACT. Corollary: positional encoding is parameter-free (sinusoidal or rotary); a learned table would have added another 131,072 and broken the count.
parameter_reconstruction.tagger: $P_m\in\mathbb{R}^{64\times256}=16{,}384$, plus LayerNorm $2\times64=128$, plus bias 64 → 16,576 EXACT. Corollary: the input is 256-wide $=2\times128$, i.e. model width — so the slot signature is per token, not per (layer, head).
parameter_reconstruction.gate: $d_g=128(k)+128(v)+128(\mathrm{PE})+64(m)+1(u)+1(a)+128(\bar\phi)=578$; $U_1\in\mathbb{R}^{128\times578}=73{,}984$, $b_1=128$, $u_r=128$, $b_r=1$ → 74,241 EXACT. Corollaries: the positional-encoding feature and the global context summary are each 128-wide, and $k_i,v_i$ enter at model width, not head width — so ONE retention score per token is shared across all 4 layers and 4 heads.
parameter_reconstruction.consolidation: $P_K,P_V\in\mathbb{R}^{128\times128}$ = 32,768, plus $\hat q_{\text{cons}}\in\mathbb{R}^{128}$ and two 128-wide biases → 33,152 EXACT.
parameter_reconstruction.why_this_matters: The reconstruction settles a question the paper leaves open and that decides its entire systems reading: the bias $\psi_i$ is a single per-token scalar applied identically at every layer and head. That is far cheaper than per-(layer,head) gating and far more restrictive — a token judged stale is suppressed everywhere at once, in every attention pattern, with no layer able to dissent. The paper never says this. See systems_implications SI-4 and todo_verify TV-3.

scale_ceiling.model_size: 793,344 base parameters (917,313 including all sleep modules). 4 layers, $d_{\text{model}}=128$, 4 heads. This is the smallest model in the corpus by roughly three orders of magnitude among papers that train a transformer at all — ch17's `Do LMs Need Sleep?` anchors at Ouro 1.4B, and the $E$-path papers use frontier APIs. [SleepGate §6.1, p.11, L659-665; Table 1, p.11]
scale_ceiling.training_data_scale: Not reported in tokens or examples. Only 45 epochs, batch 16, over synthetically generated PI sequences. The number of distinct training sequences is never stated.
scale_ceiling.vocabulary_and_task_scale: 1024 synthetic tokens; 100 entities; 500 values; sequence length $\le1024$. Chance accuracy $1/500=0.2\%$ as the paper states.
scale_ceiling.evaluation_scale: 7 depths × 200 episodes × 6 methods = 8,400 episodes total. [본서 산술] Binomial standard error at $N=200$ is 1.5 pp at $p=0.05$ and 2.7 pp at $p=0.175$, so most inter-baseline differences in Table 2 are inside one standard error — see UF-3.
scale_ceiling.realism_ceiling: Zero natural language. Zero pre-trained models. Zero real documents. The one training family that would have involved naturalistic corrections (§4.1 item 4) is incompatible with the synthetic vocabulary and reappears as future work.
scale_ceiling.in_distribution_ceiling: [본서 관찰] The failure is IN-DISTRIBUTION. §4.1 declares training PI sequences with $n\in[2,50]$ and §6.3's curriculum reaches $n=30$; every evaluated depth is therefore inside the training range. So the collapse from 97.0% at $n=10$ to 16.5% at $n=30$ is not a generalisation gap but a capacity failure on depths the model was trained on. That distinction is not drawn in the paper and it makes the proposed remedy ($d_s>64$) a conjecture about capacity rather than about coverage.
scale_ceiling.deployment_gap: Total. There is no claim in this paper that survives contact with a served model, and the paper says so. The gap this note flags additionally: the mechanism's cost is charged to the request's critical path, so the deployment question is not 'does it transfer' but 'what does one extra attention pass per micro-cycle cost at $L=128\text{K}$' — a question the toy scale cannot answer even in form, since attention/matmul cost ratios invert with $L$.

[p.15, L948-950]. open_questions.question: [note-writer] When does the trigger actually fire, and what does it cost?
open_questions.bridge_out: Eq. 16 is fully specified with three arms and three hyperparameters, and the experiments report nothing about it while §4.2/§6.3 say the sleep path ran unconditionally. Whether SleepGate is a triggered system at all is the question that decides its discriminant condition (1), and the paper does not pose it.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The experiment does not reproduce the phenomenon it claims to fix. In the paper's own Table 2, 75–93% of the baselines' predictions are values that were never in the context at all — neither the current value nor any superseded one.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] $100-\text{acc}-\text{stale}$ for Full KV Cache across $n=1..30$: 92.0, 83.5, 75.5, 81.0, 77.0, 80.0, 78.0. For H2O: 93.5, 87.0, 91.5, 85.0, 85.5, 90.0, 90.5. And Full KV Cache's accuracy series is 8.0, 9.0, 3.5, 2.0, 3.0, 1.5, 2.5 — flat near zero from $n=1$, non-monotone, and nothing like the $1/n$ that the paper's own Eq. 22 predicts or the log-linear decay-from-high that Wang & Sun report on real LLMs.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Proactive interference is defined by the paper as systematic retrieval of OVERWRITTEN values from a starting point of competence — 'The errors are not random—models systematically retrieve overwritten values' [SleepGate §1, p.2, L54-55]. The baselines here never had competence to lose and their errors are mostly not stale retrievals. So §7.1's conclusion, 'confirming that no existing cache management strategy addresses proactive interference', does not follow: the setup measures general incompetence of a 793K-parameter model on a synthetic lookup, and the effect size attributed to interference resolution is unidentified.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper's own explanation of its depth-1 result contradicts its own baseline comparison. At $n=1$ SleepGate scores 82.5% and the paper says the sleep mechanism contributes nothing there — but the Full KV Cache baseline, which is the same architecture with the same full cache at $n=1$, scores 8.0%.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'At n = 1 there is no prior value to supersede, so the sleep mechanism provides no benefit—the model relies entirely on base transformer retrieval capability.' [§7.3] and, four pages later, 'the full KV cache baseline achieves only 8.0% accuracy even at n = 1' used as evidence FOR the method [§8.1].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Both sentences cannot be true. If at $n=1$ SleepGate's score is base-transformer capability, then base-transformer capability is 82.5%, and the 8.0% baseline differs from it by something other than the sleep mechanism — namely the training objective (Eq. 19 is the evaluation metric) and the depth curriculum. A 10.3× gap at the one depth where the mechanism is declared inert localises the paper's headline effect in its training protocol, not in its architecture. This is the single most damaging internal inconsistency in the paper and it is visible from two sentences the paper itself prints.

unfavorable_facts.fact: No seeds, no confidence intervals, no significance tests, no variance of any kind. Greps for 'seed', 'confidence', 'significan' return 0 hits over the whole paper.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] At $N=200$ episodes the binomial standard error is 1.5 pp at $p=0.05$ and 2.7 pp at $p=0.175$. The standard error of the H2O–FullKV difference at $n=1$ (6.5 vs 8.0) is 2.6 pp, so that difference is under 0.6 SE. Most inter-baseline differences in Table 2 are within one standard error of zero.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: §7.2's entire baseline analysis — 'H2O performs worst', 'StreamingLLM is the best baseline' — is an ordering of numbers that are not separated by the reported sample size. The one comparison that does survive (StreamingLLM 17.5 vs FullKV 8.0 at $n=1$, 9.5 pp ≈ 2.9 SE) is also the one the paper explains away as an attention-sink artifact.

unfavorable_facts.fact: 'H2O performs worst... the lowest accuracy across all depths' is falsified by the paper's own table.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: At $n=10$, H2O scores 4.0% and Full KV Cache scores 2.0% — H2O is higher. At $n=15$ both are 3.0% — a tie. So H2O is strictly lowest at 5 of 7 depths, not all 7.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: This is a §7.2 section heading and the anchor of the paper's most-cited mechanistic claim ('cumulative attention scores are anti-correlated with freshness under PI... Retaining heavy hitters actively preserves interference'). The claim may well be right; the paper's own table does not establish it, and the table is on the facing page.

unfavorable_facts.fact: PI Slope is defined as one of the paper's three metrics and is never reported for any method.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'PI Slope: Slope of the accuracy-vs-log(n) regression line. A slope of 0 indicates perfect PI resistance; more negative slopes indicate greater susceptibility.' [§6.5]
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: It is the metric that would directly test Corollary 1's claim of $n$-independence, and it is the only one of the three declared metrics that does not appear anywhere in §7, in Table 2, or in Figure 2. The metric that could falsify the theory is the metric that goes unreported.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper contradicts itself on whether the sleep path is triggered at all.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: Algorithm 2 line 12: 'if trigger(t) then // Sleep phase (trigger per Eq. 16)'. Against §4.2 Stage 2: 'every forward pass computes both unbiased (wake) and soft-biased (sleep) logits' and §6.3: 'Each forward pass produces both unbiased logits (for the wake loss) and soft-biased logits (for the sleep loss)'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Section 3.5 spends a page and three hyperparameters ($\kappa_H=1.5$, $\rho_{\max}=0.4$, $T_{\text{cyc}}^{\max}=128$) on the adaptive trigger, §8.5 credits it ('The adaptive trigger ensures cycles only execute when beneficial'), and the experimental sections describe a system in which it does nothing. No firing count, no trigger ablation, no per-arm attribution appears anywhere. This is also the fact that makes the discriminant's condition (1) unresolvable from the paper alone.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The theoretical analysis is about a variant that was never run. Theorem 1, Corollary 1 and Proposition 1 all presuppose eviction; the evaluated soft-biasing variant evicts nothing.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'With SleepGate, after each sleep cycle, entries marked as superseded are evicted.' and 'Each sleep cycle evicts each stale entry independently with probability $p_c$.' [§5.2] Against §6.3: the soft variant was used and Stage 3 threshold calibration — the stage that sets the eviction thresholds — was omitted.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Contribution 3 in §1.2 is the theory and contribution 4 is the validation; the paper presents them as the same claim ('our preliminary experiments confirm this prediction' [§9]). They are claims about two different systems. Nothing in §7 tests anything in §5.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Theorem 1's printed bound does not follow from its own printed proof sketch.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] The proof sketch says: at most $T_{\text{cyc}}$ new entries accumulate between cycles; a stale entry survives each cycle with probability $1-p_c$; 'Summing over all $n$ stale entries and taking the expectation gives the bound.' Carrying out that sum, entry $j$ has survived $\lfloor(n-j)/T_{\text{cyc}}\rfloor$ cycles, so $\mathbb{E}[\text{stale}]=\sum_j(1-p_c)^{\lfloor(n-j)/T_{\text{cyc}}\rfloor}=T_{\text{cyc}}\,\frac{1-(1-p_c)^{n/T_{\text{cyc}}}}{p_c}\ \le\ T_{\text{cyc}}/p_c$. The printed bound is $\min\big(T_{\text{cyc}},\ \epsilon n/(1-(1-p_c)^{n/T_{\text{cyc}}})\big)$ — the same factor $(1-(1-p_c)^{n/T_{\text{cyc}}})$ appears, but in the denominator instead of the numerator, and $p_c$ is replaced by $\epsilon n$.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper's qualitative conclusion ($O(T_{\text{cyc}})$ for $p_c$ near 1) happens to be right, but by a different expression than the one printed. And the printed $\min(T_{\text{cyc}},\cdot)$ is false in the regime it is supposed to cover: at $p_c=0$ the true expected stale count is $n-1$, which exceeds $T_{\text{cyc}}$ for any $n>T_{\text{cyc}}+1$, while $\min(T_{\text{cyc}},\cdot)\le T_{\text{cyc}}$ always. A bound that holds for a gate that never evicts anything is not bounding what the theorem claims to bound.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate §5.2 Eq. 23 and proof sketch, p.10, L607-624]

unfavorable_facts.fact: A minimum is restated as a big-O of a maximum. Eq. 23 prints '$\le\min(N,\ \ldots)=O(\max(N,\epsilon\cdot n))$'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: $\min(a,b)\le\max(a,b)$, so the restatement is not an equality, and as an upper bound it is strictly weaker than the expression it is derived from. The following sentence — 'For $p_c$ close to 1 (low $\epsilon$) and moderate $N$, this is $O(N)$ regardless of $n$' — is then true of the $\min$ form for trivial reasons and not established for the $\max$ form.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate Eq. 23 and the sentence at p.10, L613-620]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Corollary 1's guarantee is vacuous at the paper's own hyperparameters.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] $p(\text{retrieve } v_n)\ge 1/(1+O(T_{\text{cyc}}))$ with the paper's fallback interval $T_{\text{cyc}}^{\max}=128$ [Table 3] gives $1/129=0.78\%$ — below every baseline in Table 2 at every depth except H2O at $n=20$ and $n=30$, and 128× below the method's own reported 99.5%.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The corollary is offered as the reason the method should work ('a constant independent of $n$, eliminating the log-linear degradation'), and instantiated at the paper's own settings it guarantees near-chance performance. A bound whose value at the paper's configuration is below the numbers it is meant to explain carries no explanatory load.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate §5.2 Eq. 24, p.10, L625-633; Table 3, p.20; Table 2, p.12]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Proposition 1's own numerical instantiation is arithmetically wrong, and the proposition has no proof.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] $|\mathcal{K}'^+|\le T_{\text{cyc}}/(\phi_e+(1-\phi_e)(1-1/\gamma_{\text{comp}}))$. At the paper's own $\phi_e=0.3,\ \gamma_{\text{comp}}=4$: denominator $=0.3+0.7\times0.75=0.825$, so the bound is $1.212\,T_{\text{cyc}}$. The paper prints 'this gives $|C'^+|\le1.67N$'. $1.67=1/0.6$ and no substitution of the stated values produces 0.6.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: This is the corpus's only state-capacity bound, and the one number the paper derives from it is wrong by 38%. It is also the only place in the paper where a capacity claim is made concrete, so a reader taking away one capacity figure takes away the wrong one. No proof or derivation accompanies the proposition.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate §5.3 Eq. 25 and the following sentence, p.10, L635-648]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 2's $n=10$ cell for SleepGate sums to more than 100%: accuracy 97.0 + stale 3.5 = 100.5.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: By the §6.5 definitions a prediction is 'accurate' if it matches the most recent value and 'stale' if it matches a superseded value; the two can coexist only if a value repeats within an episode. The paper never states whether the 500 values are sampled with or without replacement, so either the metric is undefined on a nonzero share of episodes or the cell is wrong. Every stale-rate number in the table inherits the ambiguity.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Three of the four declared training-data families were not run, and one of them could not have been.
unfavorable_facts.detail: §4.1 declares PI Sequences, Mixed-Relevance Sequences, Multi-Entity Sequences, and 'Natural Text with Synthetic Updates: Real documents augmented with "correction" statements'. §6.1 fixes the vocabulary at 1024 synthetic tokens and §6.2 evaluates single-entity synthetic PI only; §6.3 describes only a PI-depth curriculum. Family (4) is impossible without real text. Families (2) and (3) reappear as FUTURE work in §9.1 item 3 ('multi-entity PI, long-document QA with corrections').
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: §4.1 is written in the present indicative ('We construct training sequences...'), so a reader carries away a training regime three quarters of which did not happen. It also removes the paper's only claimed contact with naturalistic correction — the setting its motivation section leans on.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The consolidation module produced no number, received no gradient, and is nevertheless counted in the overhead and credited in the results.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: 33,152 parameters = 26.7% of the 123,969-parameter 'sleep overhead' in Table 1. Algorithm 1 places consolidation in Phase 3 of the hard-eviction variant; §6.3 states the soft variant was used, so no forward pass reaches Eq. 12-13 and $P_K,P_V,\hat q_{\text{cons}}$ receive no gradient in Stage 2.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: It is contribution (3) of the abstract ('a consolidation module that merges related surviving entries into compact summary representations'), it is one of the five rows of the biology mapping in Table 4 (mapped to hippocampal-neocortical replay), and §9 credits it in the sentence that reports the results: 'The three sleep-inspired modules—key decay, learned gating, and consolidation—give the model a direct mechanism for interference resolution'. It is also the module that carries the word 'consolidation', i.e. the one that makes the paper's title accurate.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate Abstract, p.1, L20-23; Table 1, p.11; Algorithm 1 lines 22-28, p.22; §6.3, p.11, L707-711; Table 4, p.21; §9, p.16, L990-991]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The gate's parameter overhead is claimed to be '< 0.01%' of the base model and is 9.36% of it in the paper's own Table 1.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'The total parameter count is negligible relative to the base model (typically < 0.01%).' [§3.3]
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] $74{,}241/793{,}344=9.358\%$ — a factor of ~936 above the stated bound. All sleep modules together: 15.626%, matching Table 1's 15.6%.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The hedge 'typically' can be read as referring to a production-scale base model, but the paper never says so and never reconciles the two figures, which sit five pages apart. A reader who takes the §3.3 sentence at face value carries away the wrong order of magnitude for the only overhead the paper actually quantifies.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The abstract's and conclusion's 'all five baselines remain below 18% across all depths' is contradicted by the paper's own table and by its own results section.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: StreamingLLM at $n=2$ is 18.0%, and §7.1 writes 'the best baseline (StreamingLLM at 18.0%)'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Small in magnitude, but it is the abstract's only universally quantified claim, it is repeated verbatim in the conclusion, and it is refuted by a number printed in the same document.

unfavorable_facts.fact: 'All baselines perform near chance (roughly 1/500 = 0.2% for random guessing) at deeper PI levels' overstates by more than an order of magnitude.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: At $n=30$ the baselines score 5.5, 4.5, 2.5, 2.0 and 0.5% — i.e. 2.5× to 27.5× the stated chance level. Several are also non-monotone in $n$ (StreamingLLM 4.0 at $n=20$ → 5.5 at $n=30$; Full KV 1.5 → 2.5; Decay Only 3.5 → 4.5), which no accumulation account predicts.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: 'Near chance' is the phrase that licenses the sentence immediately after it — 'confirming that no existing cache management strategy addresses proactive interference'. With baselines an order of magnitude above chance and moving non-monotonically, the data support neither the phrase nor the inference.

unfavorable_facts.fact: There is exactly one ablation in the paper, and it removes the component that the paper's own analysis says does not matter.
unfavorable_facts.detail: 'Decay Only' removes the gate and consolidation, leaving key decay. Absent: any ablation of the tagger, of $\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}$ (Eq. 21, the oracle-derived gate supervision), of $\mathcal{L}_{\text{compress}}$, of the trigger or any of its three arms, of $\beta_{\text{bias}}$, of $d_s$, of the curriculum with numbers, and of the $a_i$ (heavy-hitter) input feature.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper diagnoses its own failure as $d_s=64$ being too small and $\beta_{\text{bias}}=5$ saturating [§7.3, §8.5], and then lists raising $d_s$ and $\beta$ as FUTURE work [§9.1 item 2]. Both are single-hyperparameter reruns of a 917K-parameter model. The most informative missing ablation is $\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}$ / $u_i$: the gate is fed the tagger's supersession flag as an input feature AND trained by cross-entropy against it, so the null hypothesis 'the gate copies $u_i$' is never excluded.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The comparison is asymmetric in supervision while being described as fair. SleepGate is trained directly on the evaluation metric and on oracle supersession labels; the baselines are trained on neither.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: The paper's fairness claim: 'This establishes basic sequence modeling capability before introducing the sleep mechanism, and ensures a fair comparison since baselines receive the same total training budget.' [§4.2 Stage 0]. What SleepGate additionally receives: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{sleep}}=-\sum_{(k,v)\in\mathcal{A}_{\text{cur}}}\log p(v\mid k,\mathcal{K}'^+)$ — the log-likelihood of the exact quantity Table 2 scores [Eq. 19]; Stage 1 gate pre-training 'on PI sequences with ground-truth supersession labels' [§4.2 Stage 1]; and $\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}$ supervising the gate against those flags throughout Stage 2 [Eq. 21].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Equal epochs is not equal supervision. The baselines are cache policies bolted onto a plain LM objective; SleepGate is a system whose loss function is the benchmark. Combined with UF-2 (a 10.3× gap at the depth where the mechanism is declared inert), this is sufficient to explain the headline without invoking interference resolution at all — and the paper runs no arm that would separate the two explanations, e.g. the base transformer trained with $\mathcal{L}_{\text{sleep}}$ but with $\beta_{\text{bias}}=0$.

unfavorable_facts.fact: No trivial baseline and no oracle upper bound. The task is 'return the most recent value for this entity', which a pure recency prior solves exactly, and no such arm is run.
unfavorable_facts.detail: The five baselines are all cache-eviction policies (full, sliding window, H2O, StreamingLLM, decay). Absent: attend-to-last-entry; a fixed recency bias on the attention logits (i.e. SleepGate with $\pi_i$ replaced by a monotone function of age, which would separate 'learned content-dependent gating' from 'any recency signal at all'); and oracle eviction using the ground-truth supersession labels the training pipeline already computes, which would give the achievable ceiling.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: This is the same defect the book records across the $E$-path — the missing arm is always the cheapest and most obvious one (→ ch27 판정 5, '빠진 대조군은 매번 가장 싸고 가장 자명한 baseline이다'). Here the oracle arm is not merely cheap: the labels already exist inside Stage 1.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The gate's input feature vector includes the H2O heavy-hitter statistic, which the paper's own analysis identifies as anti-correlated with the right answer, and the paper never remarks on it.
unfavorable_facts.detail: Eq. 5 includes $a_i$, 'the cumulative attention received by this entry (analogous to the "heavy hitter" score of Zhang et al. [2023])'. §7.2 then explains H2O's failure: 'cumulative attention scores are anti-correlated with freshness under PI: the model attends most to the entries it has seen most often, which are precisely the stale values. Retaining heavy hitters actively preserves interference.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Either the feature is useful (and §7.2's mechanism claim is wrong) or it is anti-correlated (and it is a liability the gate must learn to invert). The paper asserts both and tests neither. Removing $a_i$ from Eq. 5 is a one-line ablation.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate Eq. 5 and surrounding text, p.6, L262-269; §7.2, p.13, L855-857]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The failure is in-distribution. Every evaluated depth lies inside the training range, so the collapse at $n\ge15$ is not a generalisation gap.
unfavorable_facts.detail: §4.1 specifies PI training sequences with $n\in[2,50]$; §6.3's curriculum reaches $n=30$ by the final epoch; evaluation depths are $\{1,2,5,10,15,20,30\}$. (§4.1 and §6.3 also disagree with each other about the maximum, 50 vs 30.)
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper frames the cliff as a capacity limit to be fixed by a larger $d_s$, which is plausible; but it never states that the model was trained on exactly the depths where it fails, which is the fact that makes the capacity reading the only remaining one and rules out under-exposure. It also means the curriculum's final stage was training on sequences the model ends up scoring 16.5% on.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The computational-overhead paragraph omits the second forward pass that Algorithm 1 and Figure 1 both mandate, and calls the remainder 'negligible' without measurement.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'Each sleep micro-cycle requires a forward pass through the gate network for every cache entry... this is $O(C\cdot d_g\cdot d_h)$ per cycle—negligible compared to a transformer forward pass, but non-zero.' [§8.5]
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] At the paper's configuration the gate over the whole cache is ~6.2% of one full-sequence forward — small but not negligible, and the comparison as written (per-entry gate cost vs a whole forward pass) is the wrong ratio, since the gate runs over all $C$ entries. The omitted re-read adds ~44% (attention-only) to ~100% (full second pass).
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: This is the only cost sentence in the paper, and it accounts for the cheapest of the three cost terms while omitting the most expensive. Under STC-STYLE-NOTATION §6.4 rule 3, a method whose cost cells are empty cannot be described as efficient; here the paper does not describe itself as efficient but does describe its overhead as negligible, which is the same move.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate §8.5 'Computational Overhead', p.16, L973-976; Algorithm 1 line 20, p.22; Figure 1 caption, p.4]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Key decay is multiplicative on the key vector, so it is not a monotone suppression operator, and at the paper's own $\lambda=0.01$ its magnitude is at most 6.7%.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: [본서 산술] $k_i\leftarrow k_i(1+\mathrm{age}_i)^{-\lambda}$ with $\lambda=0.01$: at the maximum age of 1023 the factor is $1024^{-0.01}=0.933$. Since the logit is $q_t^\top k_i/\sqrt d$, scaling $k_i$ by $c<1$ scales the logit by $c$ — which pushes it toward zero. Entries whose logit is POSITIVE are suppressed; entries whose logit is NEGATIVE are boosted relative to the softmax mean. Decay therefore compresses the attention distribution toward uniform rather than monotonically down-weighting old entries.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Table 4 maps this operator to synaptic homeostasis and asserts it 'preserves relative importance while reducing absolute interference' [§1.1, Table 4] — but a multiplicative shrink of the logit does not preserve relative importance under softmax; it reduces the temperature-scaled contrast in both directions. It is also the operator the paper elsewhere treats as the persistent part of its mechanism, and its own ablation puts it at baseline level (≤12.5%), which is consistent with the 6.7% magnitude computed here.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate Algorithm 1 lines 3-4, p.22; Table 3 'Decay rate $\lambda$ 0.01', p.20; §1.1, p.2, L72-76; Table 4 row 1, p.21; §7.2, p.13, L861-864]

unfavorable_facts.fact: No code, no data, no released artifact, no seeds — for a result that is a 917K-parameter model on a synthetic vocabulary and therefore reproducible in minutes if any of these existed.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Among the papers in this corpus this is the one whose reproduction cost is lowest by orders of magnitude, and it is the one that supplies the least reproduction material. Letta STC released a repository; this paper releases nothing.
unfavorable_facts.source: [grep 'github' over the full text: 0 hits; no data/code availability statement anywhere]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper's own three-module enumeration changes between the introduction and the conclusion.
unfavorable_facts.detail: §1.2 and §3 name the three modules as (1) conflict-aware temporal tagger, (2) forgetting gate, (3) consolidation module. §9 names them as 'key decay, learned gating, and consolidation'. Key decay is Phase 1 of Algorithm 1 and is not one of the three modules in §3; the tagger has vanished.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: It matters because the tagger is the module that supplies $u_i$, which is both an input feature and the supervision target of $\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}$ — i.e. the module through which the oracle signal enters. Dropping it from the conclusion's enumeration removes from the summary the component most responsible for the result being easy.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Presentation defects in the vendored text: Appendix B ('Pseudocode for Training Loop') is an empty heading with Algorithm 2 appearing after Appendix C's table; Figure 2's x-axis reads 'Number of Prior Updates (PI Depth)' while its tick values are $n$ (total updates), so at $n=1$ the axis claims one prior update where §7.3 says there are none; the Gumbel-softmax relaxation is used in §3.3 with no citation while Jang et al. 2017 sits uncited in the bibliography (the only uncited entry of 46).
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Individually minor. Together with UF-8, UF-9, UF-11 and UF-15 they establish that the paper's numeric and structural claims were not checked against each other, which is the reason this note verifies every arithmetic statement rather than quoting any of them.
unfavorable_facts.source: [SleepGate App. B heading, p.20, L1228-1230; Algorithm 2, p.23; Figure 2 axis, p.13, L836; §3.3, p.6, L292-294; References, p.18, L1085-1086]

bio_CLS_path.citations: ELEVEN — Tononi & Cirelli 2006 and 2014 (synaptic homeostasis), Diekelmann & Born 2010, Rasch & Born 2013, Ellenbogen et al. 2006, Abel et al. 2013, Staresina et al. 2015 (spindles/ripples), Berry & Davis 2014 and Davis & Zhong 2017 (active forgetting), Kumaran, Hassabis & McClelland 2016 (CLS updated), Tadros et al. 2022, González et al. 2020.
bio_CLS_path.finding: This is the most substantive biological engagement in the corpus, and it is qualitatively different from the corpus's usual pattern: §1.1 is a mechanism-level account (SHY → downscaling; SWS replay → selective consolidation; dopaminergic active forgetting) and Appendix C's Table 4 maps five biological mechanisms onto five modules with a 'Functional Correspondence' column. Where Letta STC's silence map row reads '생물 ✗ (제목에 빌려 씀)', this paper's reads '생물 ○, 세 경로 ✗'.
bio_CLS_path.relation_to_this_book_s_bio_corpus: It cites neither of the book's two bio papers, but it cites their immediate neighbours from the same laboratory: González et al. 2020 (eLife 9:e51005, 'Can sleep protect memories from catastrophic forgetting?') shares authors Delanois and Bazhenov with the book's `sleep prevents catastrophic forgetting` (Golden, Delanois, Sanda, Bazhenov, PLoS Comput Biol 2022), and Tadros et al. 2022 (Nature Communications) is Bazhenov lab as well. So all three of its sleep-replay-in-ANN citations come from one group, and the specific paper this book vendored is not among them. PAD (eLife 2022) is absent.
bio_CLS_path.what_it_does_NOT_do: It does not test any biological prediction. Table 4 is a correspondence table, not an experiment: no ablation is organised around a biological hypothesis, no biological claim is used to make a falsifiable prediction about the model, and the sleep-stage hierarchy of §8.3 is offered as a hypothesis with no experiment attached. The argument comes along with the name, but stops at analogy.

cross_path_citations.what_it_DOES_engage_fully: The serving and long-context literature, exhaustively and accurately: Longformer, sparse transformers, H2O, StreamingLLM, FastGen (Ge et al. 2024), Infini-attention, KVQuant, PagedAttention, GQA, RULER, LongBench, Lost-in-the-Middle. Five of these are run as baselines. This is the one community that every other paper in the corpus ignores and the one this book's reader belongs to.
cross_path_citations.monograph_implication: Two things follow. (i) The silence finding is confirmed at its sharpest — a paper titled after sleep-dependent memory consolidation, published 2026-03, cites none of the nine papers this book identifies as the category, including the one that named it 11 months earlier. (ii) The silence map needs a new ROW SHAPE, because this paper's pattern is the inverse of every existing row: bio ○, KV-cache/serving ○○, $E$ ancestors only, $W$ adjacent families only, $\Theta$ ✗, sleep-time-compute corpus ✗. The book has been describing a field in which the biology is borrowed without its argument; here the argument is borrowed carefully and the field is ignored. Both are failures of the same kind — communities that do not read each other — and printing them side by side is stronger than printing either alone (→ ch23 §23.8, ch11 §11.7).

systems_implications.preamble: This is the only paper in the corpus whose mechanism lands inside the attention kernel, so it is the only one that can be translated into the reader's world without extrapolation. The translation is mixed: the soft variant is the cheapest possible intervention, and the parts the paper leaves for future work are the ones that break the serving stack. Items marked [PAPER] are the paper's; [본서 산술] and [본서 추론] are this note's, per STC-STYLE-NOTATION §6.2.

items.claim: The retention score is ONE scalar per token, shared across all layers and all heads. The paper never says this; it follows from its parameter counts.
items.grounding: [본서 산술] $P_m\in\mathbb{R}^{64\times256}$ requires a 128-wide key input, and $d_g=578$ decomposes only if $k_i,v_i,\mathrm{PE},\bar\phi$ each enter at $d_{\text{model}}=128$ rather than at head width 32. Both counts match Table 1 exactly. Consequence for serving: the whole mechanism is one length-$L$ fp16 vector per request, not $L\times L_{\text{layer}}\times n_{\text{heads}}$. That is 2 bytes per token per request — negligible — and it makes the soft variant trivially compatible with GQA, which the paper worries about in §8.5. Consequence for quality: a token judged stale is suppressed in every head at every layer simultaneously, including heads doing syntax rather than retrieval, with no layer able to dissent. [본서 추론] That is the sharpest reason to doubt transfer to a pre-trained model, and it is a different reason from the one the paper gives ($d_s$ capacity).

items.claim: The soft-bias mechanism itself is the cheapest intervention available in an attention kernel. An additive per-key pre-softmax bias is the same slot that ALiBi and relative-position biases already occupy.
items.grounding: [본서 추론] grounded in Eq. 11. The bias enters as $\exp(q^\top k_i/\sqrt d+\psi_i)$, so a fused kernel needs one extra length-$L$ vector loaded alongside K, at 2 B/entry (bf16) against 2·$d_{\text{head}}$·2 B of K+V per entry per head. At $d_{\text{head}}=128$ that is +0.4% of KV traffic per head, and by SI-1 the vector is shared across heads, so it is loaded once. This is the favourable half of the systems reading and it should be stated as clearly as the unfavourable half.

items.claim: The expensive kernel term is not the bias — it is the gate's INPUT features. Two of them are quantities a fused attention kernel does not produce.
items.grounding: [본서 추론] Eq. 5 requires (a) $a_i$, the cumulative attention mass received by each cache entry, i.e. column sums of the attention matrix, and (b) via Eq. 14 the per-head attention entropy $H_t$. FlashAttention-style kernels never materialise the attention matrix, so column sums require either a second pass or cross-tile atomic accumulation — this is the same cost that H2O implementations pay and it is well known in that literature. Entropy is the better case: since $H_t=\log Z-\frac1Z\sum_i s_i\,\ell_i$ with $s_i=\exp(\ell_i)$, it CAN be accumulated online with the same rescaling trick used for $\sum_i s_i v_i$, at the cost of one extra accumulator channel per query row. So the entropy trigger is implementable in a fused kernel but requires a kernel change; the heavy-hitter feature requires a pass or an atomic. The paper prices neither.

items.claim: The cost is charged to the request's critical path, not to idle time. This is a serving statement, not only a taxonomic one.
items.grounding: [PAPER] 'These components are activated periodically during inference in "sleep micro-cycles"' [Abstract, p.1] and Algorithm 2 places the sleep branch inside the per-token loop. [본서 산술] At the paper's configuration one extra attention pass is ~+44% of a full-sequence forward and a full second pass is +100%. At production sequence lengths the ratio moves further against the method, because attention grows as $L^2$ while the matmul term grows as $L$: at $L=128\text{K}$ on a model with $d=4096$ and 32 layers the attention term dominates, so re-running attention approaches doubling the prefill. Whatever this mechanism is, it is not a way of moving work off the request.

items.claim: The augmented cache adds per-entry metadata whose byte cost the paper never states, and whose scoping the paper's own equations leave ambiguous.
items.grounding: [본서 산술] Under SI-1's reading (one signature per token at model width, bf16): $\approx135$ B/token of metadata against $2\,d\,L_{\text{layer}}\cdot2$ B of KV, i.e. +6.6% at the paper's toy config and $\approx+0.05\%$ at an 8B-class config where KV per token is far larger. Under the literal reading of Eq. 2, which scopes $\mathcal{K}^+$ over $C^{\ell,h}$, the same metadata is materialised per (layer, head) and the figure rises by $L_{\text{layer}}\times n_{\text{heads}}$. The paper does not resolve which, and the two readings differ by more than an order of magnitude in the only capacity number a serving engineer would care about.

items.claim: Hard eviction breaks PagedAttention's block invariants; the paper's expectation of compatibility is not grounded.
items.grounding: [본서 추론] against [PAPER] §8.5's 'We expect compatibility since SleepGate operates on the logical cache structure'. PagedAttention allocates the cache in fixed-size blocks (16 tokens is the common default) and addresses them through a block table. Evicting scattered entries produces partially-valid blocks, which requires either a per-entry validity mask threaded into the kernel (giving up the density that makes paging cheap) or a compaction pass that rewrites the block table and moves KV bytes. Neither is free, and neither is 'logical'.

items.claim: Consolidation is incompatible with cross-request prefix caching and with position-encoding schemes applied at write time, and this is the more serious of the two.
items.grounding: [본서 추론] Eq. 12 produces a synthetic $(k^*_m,v^*_m)$ that corresponds to no token. Two consequences. (i) Prefix caching keys a cached KV block on the token prefix that produced it; once the cache contains entries that are content-dependent weighted averages, it is no longer a function of the prefix, so cross-request reuse is dead for any request that has slept. That removes the single largest serving optimisation available to long-context workloads — the same optimisation ch25 판정 2 identifies as the one that decides the $E$-path's amortisation argument. (ii) With RoPE the rotation is baked into $k_i$ at write time, so a weighted average of rotated keys is a key at no well-defined position; the paper's recency-weighted pool over $\tilde\tau_i$ does not repair this because the weighting is on the pooling coefficients, not on the rotation.

items.claim: Quantised KV caches interact with the gate through its inputs, not through the bias.
items.grounding: [본서 추론]. Eq. 5 feeds $k_i$ and $v_i$ into the gate. With an int4/int8 cache those must be dequantised to score, or the gate must be trained on quantised inputs; and the gate's discrimination is exactly a fine-grained comparison among near-identical entries for the same slot — the regime where quantisation error is most likely to matter. The paper's §8.5 lists KVQuant compatibility as expected. [본서 판단] The expectation is untested and the mechanism is one where it is least likely to hold.

items.claim: The state here is HOT-tier and per-request, which is a third coordinate distinct from both this book's and Neural Memory's memory-centric opportunities.
items.grounding: [본서 추론] against ch29 표 29-2. Neural Memory's coordinate is HBM read-modify-write bandwidth for a session-lifetime $W$ at token granularity; this book's is warm-tier random-read deadline and write endurance for a user-lifetime $\Theta$ delta at sleep-round granularity. SleepGate's is neither: a per-request, request-lifetime object already resident in HBM, touched at micro-cycle granularity, with no persistence and no staging. It therefore adds a third row to 표 29-2 rather than filling either existing one — which independently supports ch29's refusal to weld the two monographs' conclusions, by showing that 'memory-centric opportunity' resolves into at least three unrelated coordinates.

items.claim: The one transferable measurement idea is the stale retrieval rate.
items.grounding: [본서 판단] §6.5 defines a metric that partitions errors into 'retrieved a superseded value' and 'everything else'. No $E$-path paper in this corpus reports that partition, and it is precisely the number that would diagnose Zep's knowledge-update regression (76.9→74.4 on gpt-4o-mini) and Mem0's loss to full-context (66.88 vs 72.90) — both of which are currently unexplained because the papers report only accuracy (→ ch15). The metric costs nothing to add to an existing eval harness. This is the item ch29 or ch30 should carry forward from this paper, and it is worth more than the mechanism.

items.claim: The trigger, if it were real, would be the corpus's only proposal to schedule maintenance off the model's own uncertainty — and it converges with SCM without either paper knowing.
items.grounding: [본서 관찰] Eq. 16's arms are attention entropy above a running threshold, conflict density above $\rho_{\max}$, and a periodic fallback. SCM triggers its cycles on buffer entropy, conflict density, and elapsed time [SCM §3.6] (→ ch15). Two papers, different layers, no shared citation, same three signals. [본서 판단] That convergence is evidence that the scheduling question has a natural answer independent of what is being scheduled, and it is a better argument for the frequency-continuum idea than Nested Learning's (→ ch18) because it is an empirical coincidence rather than a notational one.

items.claim: For the serving reader the correct one-sentence summary is: this is a learned, content-dependent attention mask, trained end-to-end, applied uniformly across layers and heads.
items.grounding: [본서 판단] grounded in SG-5 and SI-1. Everything else — the trigger, the tagger, the consolidation module, the biology table, the theory — is either unexercised, oracle-supplied, or about a different system. Saying it this way is not a dismissal: a learned attention mask is a real and useful primitive, it sits in the same family as H2O and StreamingLLM but with a learned score instead of a fixed rule, and it is the first thing in this corpus a serving engineer could implement in an afternoon. It is simply not a write to any layer, and therefore not sleep-time compute.

book_impact.summary: Confirms the book's spine thesis and four specific verdicts, more sharply than any single paper in the existing corpus. Threatens no verdict. Threatens two pieces of the book's APPARATUS — ch11 §11.2.4's claim to have exactly two grey zones, and the KV↔$W$ Rosetta row's implicit claim that append-only losslessness is a property of caches rather than a design choice — and forces a mechanical recount from 29 to 30. Overturns nothing. It also supplies ch29 with the corpus's only kernel-level material and ch23 with a partial counter-example that must be printed.
